title: Prohibition on sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or occupancy levels
requirement: No one may sell, license or otherwise provide to Berkeley landlords a coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. Landlords may not use such an algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels. A coordinated pricing algorithm is one that uses nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old.
key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (each month and each unit is a separate violation)
coverage_conditions: All residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley, and anyone selling or licensing coordinated pricing algorithms to Berkeley landlords.
exemptions: Not covered: products that publish aggregated, anonymous rental data without recommending rents or terms; products used to set rent or income limits under government affordable housing guidelines; and products used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing or training for software development (as long as competitor data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated). The chapter does not regulate the amount of rent a landlord may charge.
